posts.text: Nov 3: Crypto-mining and computing-hosting shares rebounded about 14.6% while Bitcoin rose about 1%, near $77,000. The nine had fallen sharply over the prior 20 sessions. No same-day company cause is established; consistent with a rebound from lower prices.
posts.source_title: Crypto-mining and computing-hosting shares rebounded about 14.6% while Bitcoin stayed near $77,000; the same-day cause is not established.

posts.text: Nov 3: Marvell rose slightly and Lumentum fell slightly while the optical group gained about 5.1%. Lumentum closed 12.1% below the Marvell share package, wider than 11.3%. Analyst targets cut to $225 from $400 and $350. Fits deal-closing risk, not weak Lumentum.
posts.source_title: Lumentum's discount to the Marvell share package widened to 12.1% on Nov. 3 even as optical peers rallied; the pattern remains more consistent with deal-closing risk than weak operations.

posts.text: Nov 3: Lattice Semiconductor posted record quarterly sales of $291M, up 118% year over year. Fabrinet sales rose 51% to $1.47B and guided above forecasts. Lam Research said 2027 factory-equipment spending should exceed $200B. Company-specific gains, not one chip trade.
posts.source_title: Lattice Semiconductor and Fabrinet rose on their own strong sales, showing the chip rebound was not one uniform trade.

posts.text: Nov 3: Sysco's sales missed forecasts, and it said restaurants are buying less; full-year sales growth will be at the low end of its range. Performance Food Group and US Foods fell about 4% with no separate news. ADM and Keurig Dr Pepper drops lack confirmed cause.
posts.source_title: Restaurant suppliers fell after Sysco's softer traffic warning; ADM and Keurig Dr Pepper dropped on separate reports with unresolved drivers.

posts.text: Nov 3: Energy shares split by business. Oil producers and drillers stayed weak after Iran-deal hopes lowered oil; no actual supply change confirmed. Refiners were split and mostly better; pipelines split. Broad energy group fell about 4.4% over the week.
posts.source_title: Energy shares split by business on Nov. 3; oil producers and drillers stayed weak after Iran-deal hopes lowered oil, but no actual supply change is confirmed.

posts.text: Nov 3: Apple beat sales and profit forecasts but said its holiday-quarter share of sales left after direct costs will fall. Stock fell about 2.1%; Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon, and Alphabet rose. Memory costs are one cited pressure; the drop didn't spread.
posts.source_title: Apple's holiday-quarter warning that it will keep less profit from each sale, not a sales miss, sent its stock lower on Nov. 3 while other large technology shares rose.

posts.text: Nov 3: The S&P 500 rebound was narrow. Beaten-down electrical, power, and AI-equipment groups led; real estate was nearly flat and all five rail companies fell. Over 20 sessions, real estate averaged +6.2%, rail +7.5%. Rotation, not a broad market turn.
posts.source_title: Nov. 3's bounce came from previously beaten-down electrical, power, and AI-equipment groups, while the real-estate and rail groups that had supported the index did not lead.

posts.text: Nov 3: Chip-equipment, optical, and memory shares rose sharply after a month-long slide. Packaging/test/factory suppliers +6.5%, optical +5.1%, large chipmakers +3.1%, memory/hard-disk +3.0%. Groups were still down 18%–37% over prior 20 sessions. Several drivers, not one cause.
posts.source_title: Chip-equipment, optical, and memory shares rose sharply on Nov. 3 after a month-long slide, but the evidence points to several drivers rather than one common cause.

posts.text: $SHOP grew revenue 32% and delivered a 22% free cash flow margin, but sales slightly missed estimates. Q4 gross profit is guided to grow more slowly than revenue. The question is how much of that sales growth converts into profit.
posts.source_title: Shopify shares fall after strong sales growth and a softer profit outlook; a separate filing allows future share and debt sales.
